verdict.summary: Composio has no managed Pipedrive app, so you have to register your own from a developer sandbox account. A private app needs no review and any Pipedrive company can install it from a direct link. A public Marketplace app must pass Pipedrive's review, which can take up to 21 business days. You cannot switch between public and private after you create the app.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for a private app; 1-3 days for a public app (listing assets, legal pages, demo video)
verdict.time_to_first_connection: 30-60 min once you have the sandbox account
verdict.approval_wait: none for a private app; up to 21 business days for a public app's review

gates.name: Developer sandbox + newly created app
gates.unlocks: You can create a public or private app in Developer Hub, get the client_id and client_secret, and connect your own sandbox company through Composio.
limits: Developer Hub only appears for developer sandbox accounts
Only one callback URL per app
Access token lasts 60 minutes; the refresh token expires after 60 days without use
gates.time_to_reach: 30-60 min after you have the sandbox account

gates.name: Private app (direct, unlisted install link)
gates.unlocks: Any Pipedrive company you send the link to can install the app and authorize it. There is no approval process and no Marketplace listing.
limits: Not listed in the Marketplace; users install only through the direct link
No install cap found in the docs reviewed
The company's shared daily API token budget and per-token burst limits apply
If you created a public app, the docs don't say whether anyone besides you can install it before approval
gates.time_to_reach: Right after Gate 1 if you chose a private app

gates.name: Approved public app (published in the Marketplace)
gates.unlocks: Anyone can find and install the app from the Pipedrive Marketplace.
limits: Approved apps are unlisted by default; you must publish manually from Developer Hub
Rejection reasons must be fixed before you resubmit
Requires a demo video, test accounts, legal pages and listing assets
gates.time_to_reach: Up to 21 business days of review after submission, plus any resubmission rounds

steps.title: Request a Pipedrive developer sandbox account
steps.detail: Request a developer sandbox account from Pipedrive's developer site. Developer Hub (where you create apps) is only visible in sandbox accounts.
gotchas: Without a sandbox account you won't see Developer Hub at all.

steps.title: Open Developer Hub
steps.detail: In the sandbox account, open the Settings menu under your company name and choose Developer Hub from the drop-down menu.

steps.title: Decide: public or private app
steps.detail: Choose a private app if a direct install link is enough. It skips review, and any Pipedrive company can install it from the link. Choose a public app only if you need a Marketplace listing. Public apps must be approved, and Composio's guide notes approval is needed before you can use one.
gotchas: You can't change the app type later in Developer Hub. Changing it means creating a new app, which also gives you a new client_id.

steps.title: Create the app and fill in Basic info
steps.detail: Click the green "Create an app" button, pick public or private, and fill in the two required fields on the Basic info tab: App name and OAuth Callback URL. Saving takes you to the OAuth & access scopes tab.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Only one callback URL is allowed per app, so use the exact URL shown in your Composio auth config.
Composio's catalog lists https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add as the default, but newer flows may use a v3 path. Copy the URL from your Composio dashboard.
Public app names must be unique in the Marketplace and must not suggest that Pipedrive built the app.

steps.title: Select only the scopes you need
steps.detail: On the OAuth & access scopes tab, turn on the read or full variant for each resource your agent uses, for example deals:read or contacts:full. An agent can map your planned endpoints to the minimum scopes using Pipedrive's endpoint-to-scope table. Leave Installation URL empty unless installs start outside the Marketplace.
gotchas: Composio's default list (contacts, leads, mail, activities, products, projects, all :full) is broad. Trim it.
Users must accept or deny all scopes at once, so extra scopes add friction.
The admin scope requires the installing user to be a company admin.

steps.title: Paste client_id and client_secret into Composio
steps.detail: Copy client_id and client_secret from the OAuth & access scopes tab into a Composio auth config for the pipedrive toolkit. Make the scopes in Composio match the ones you enabled in Developer Hub.
gotchas: client_id can never be changed. client_secret can be regenerated without invalidating existing user tokens.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection. It sends you to https://oauth.pipedrive.com/oauth/authorize, then exchanges the code at https://oauth.pipedrive.com/oauth/token using HTTP Basic auth. Check that a call such as fetching the current user succeeds and that the token refreshes after 60 minutes.
gotchas: The authorization code expires in 5 minutes.
A 401 'unauthorized access' from the authorize endpoint usually means a wrong client_id.
If a refresh token goes unused for 60 days, the user has to reauthorize.

steps.title: Share the private app with users (private route)
steps.detail: For a private app, send users the direct installation link, or let them connect through your Composio flow. No review is needed. Plan around the company-wide daily token budget and the per-token burst limits.
gotchas: Requests return 429 once a company's daily token budget runs out, until the daily reset.

steps.title: Prepare listing assets and legal pages (public route)
steps.detail: Draft a Terms of Service page, a Privacy Policy page, a pricing page link and a support contact. Prepare a distinctive app icon (PNG/JPG, 1:1, at least 256x256 px, max 10 MB) and 3-5 listing images (16:10, 1280x800 or larger). Check that the app name doesn't clash with existing Marketplace listings.

steps.title: Record the demo video and set up test accounts
steps.detail: Record a demo video that explains how each permission and scope is used and shows the key functionality. Provide working test accounts and a contact person for the review team.
gotchas: The app must use OAuth 2.0, must not store user API tokens, must refresh tokens after 60 minutes, must request only the scopes it needs, and must respect rate limits.

steps.title: Accept the Developer Partner Agreement and send to review
steps.detail: Read and accept Pipedrive's Developer Partner Agreement. Install and test the app, preview the listing, then click Send to review in Developer Hub.

steps.title: Wait for Pipedrive's review
steps.detail: Pipedrive says public app reviews can take up to 21 business days. If the app is rejected, the email lists the reasons, and you must fix them before resubmitting.
steps.est_time: Up to 21 business days per round

steps.title: Publish the approved app
steps.detail: Approved apps stay unlisted by default. Publish the app manually from Developer Hub to make it appear in the Marketplace.

requirements.detail: Required before Developer Hub is visible.

requirements.item: Exactly one OAuth Callback URL matching Composio's callback
requirements.detail: The redirect_uri sent in the authorize request must match the registered callback.

requirements.item: Terms of Service and Privacy Policy pages
requirements.detail: Both are required for public app approval.

requirements.item: Unique app name, icon, 3-5 listing images, pricing link, support contact
requirements.detail: Icon: 1:1, at least 256x256 px. Images: 16:10, 1280x800 or larger.

requirements.item: Demo video, test accounts, reviewer contact
requirements.detail: The video must explain how scopes and permissions are used.
OAuth 2.0 as the primary auth, no stored user API tokens, token refresh every 60 minutes, minimal scopes, rate-limit handling.
Must be accepted before you submit.

scopes.effect: Always enabled for every app; can't be removed.
Read-only access to the mapped endpoints. Choose these where you can to keep the consent request small.
Read and write access. Composio's defaults use :full for six resources; trim to what you need, because reviewers check that scopes are necessary.
The installing user must be a company admin. The app must still handle non-admin installers, for example when creating pipelines, stages or custom fields.

blockers.symptom: Developer Hub doesn't appear in Settings
blockers.cause: You're signed in to a regular Pipedrive account, not a developer sandbox.
blockers.fix: Request a developer sandbox account and create the app from it.

blockers.symptom: You need to switch an app between public and private
blockers.cause: The app type can't be changed after creation.
blockers.fix: Create a new app of the right type and update Composio with the new client_id and client_secret.

blockers.symptom: redirect_uri mismatch or a failed callback during connection
blockers.cause: The registered callback doesn't match Composio's callback (for example, a v1 vs v3 path), or a placeholder URL is still saved.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config into OAuth Callback URL. Only one is allowed.

blockers.cause: Missing legal pages or assets, a non-unique name, unnecessary scopes, or a missing or unclear demo video.
blockers.fix: Fix every reason listed in the rejection email, then resubmit.

blockers.symptom: Approved app doesn't show up in the Marketplace
blockers.cause: Approved apps are unlisted by default.
blockers.fix: Publish the app manually from Developer Hub.

blockers.symptom: Connections break after a long period of inactivity
blockers.cause: The refresh token expired after 60 days without use.
blockers.fix: Have the user reauthorize. Refresh tokens regularly to keep the window open.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Pipedrive, so you must register your own in Developer Hub and paste its client_id and client_secret into a Composio auth config. Set the OAuth Callback URL to the exact callback shown in your Composio dashboard. The catalog lists https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, but check the dashboard. A private app works right away for any company you share it with. A public app must pass Pipedrive's review before Composio users can rely on it. Trim the default :full scopes to what your agent uses.

evidence.claim: The developer sandbox account is requested through Pipedrive's developer site.
evidence.quote: Request a developer sandbox account to get access to the Developer Hub

evidence.claim: Developer Hub is opened from the company Settings menu, under the company name of the sandbox account.
evidence.quote: choose Developer Hub from the drop-down menu

evidence.claim: Creating an app means clicking Create an app and then choosing a public or private app.
evidence.quote: click on the green “Create an app” button

evidence.claim: The public/private choice cannot be changed later in Developer Hub.
evidence.quote: Do pick your app type carefully, as it cannot be changed later on Developer Hub.

evidence.claim: Basic info requires App name and OAuth Callback URL; client_id and client_secret appear on the OAuth & access scopes tab.
evidence.quote: This tab has two required fields – App name and OAuth Callback URL.

evidence.claim: Only one callback URL is allowed per app; a placeholder must be replaced before submission.
evidence.quote: Keep in mind that we allow only one callback URL per app

evidence.claim: The callback URL is the OAuth redirect_uri.
evidence.quote: Technically, a callback URL is the same thing as an OAuth redirect_uri.

evidence.claim: client_id cannot be changed; client_secret can be regenerated without invalidating existing user tokens.
evidence.quote: The client_id cannot be refreshed or changed for existing apps.

evidence.claim: Scopes are set on the OAuth & access scopes tab; Installation URL is optional.
evidence.quote: Use it when you need to start app authorization outside of the Marketplace

evidence.claim: The authorize endpoint is https://oauth.pipedrive.com/oauth/authorize, and redirect_uri must match the registered callback.
evidence.quote: The callback URL you provided when you registered your app.

evidence.claim: The token endpoint is https://oauth.pipedrive.com/oauth/token, authenticated with HTTP Basic auth.
evidence.quote: your request has to be authenticated via HTTP Basic Auth with the values of the client_id and the client_secret

evidence.claim: The authorization code expires after 5 minutes.
evidence.quote: the authorization_code expires in 5 minutes

evidence.claim: Access tokens last 60 minutes and must be refreshed.
evidence.quote: access_token expires after 60 minutes.

evidence.claim: A refresh token expires after 60 days without use.
evidence.quote: refresh_token will expire if it isn't used in 60 days

evidence.claim: PKCE support was not confirmed in the docs reviewed.
base scope is always enabled.
evidence.quote: This is the default permission that is always enabled for all apps.

evidence.claim: Scopes have read and full variants per resource, each mapped to endpoints.
evidence.quote: Here's our mapping of API endpoints to access scopes

evidence.claim: The admin scope requires the installing user to have admin rights.
evidence.quote: requires the user who is installing an app (from the Pipedrive's Marketplace), to have admin rights within the company

evidence.claim: Users accept or deny all scopes together.
evidence.quote: The user has the option to either accept or deny all scopes.

evidence.claim: Each new public app must pass the approval process, submitted via Send to review.
evidence.quote: Each new public app submitted to the Pipedrive Marketplace has to pass our approval process

evidence.claim: Requires ToS, Privacy Policy, unique name and icon, 3-5 images, pricing link and support contact.
evidence.quote: Your app has a Privacy Policy webpage of a legal document

evidence.claim: Review requires a demo video explaining scope use, plus test accounts and a contact.
evidence.quote: Provide our team with a demo video in which you explain the usage of permissions and scopes

evidence.claim: Technical requirements: OAuth 2.0, no stored API tokens, refresh after 60 minutes, minimal scopes, rate limits.
evidence.quote: Your app refreshes the access token once its 60-minute lifetime expires

evidence.claim: Icon is 1:1, at least 256x256 px, max 10 MB; listing images are 16:10, 1280x800 or larger, up to 5.
evidence.quote: 1:1 aspect ratio

evidence.claim: Public app reviews may take up to 21 business days.
evidence.quote: public app reviews may take up to 21 business days

evidence.claim: Rejection reasons must be resolved before resubmission.
evidence.quote: Before the app can be submitted again, you’ll need to resolve the reason(s) for the rejection

evidence.claim: Approved apps are unlisted by default and must be published manually.
evidence.quote: The app is unlisted from the Marketplace by default after approval.

evidence.claim: App names must be unique and must not imply Pipedrive built the app.
evidence.quote: Your app name is unique and isn’t similar to another app in the Marketplace

evidence.claim: Private apps skip approval and can be shared with any company through a direct unlisted link.
evidence.quote: The app doesn't have to go through the app approval process

evidence.claim: Composio notes a public Pipedrive app must be approved before use; a private app avoids review.
evidence.quote: It needs to be approved by the Pipedrive team before you start using it.

evidence.claim: Composio's guide says the public app name must be unique and the callback field should be set to the Composio callback URL.
evidence.quote: Since this is a public app, the name must be unique across all applications

evidence.claim: Composio's catalog lists default redirect https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add; confirm the callback in the dashboard.
evidence.quote: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add

evidence.claim: The authorize endpoint is live and returns 401 for a fake client_id.
evidence.quote: unauthorized access

evidence.claim: Burst limits are per token over a rolling 2-second window (e.g. 80 on Lite, 480 on Ultimate).
evidence.quote: 80 requests per 2 seconds

evidence.quote: Review and understand the requirements of the Pipedrive Developer Partner Agreement

evidence.claim: No install cap for unreviewed public apps was found.

open_questions: Can other companies install an unapproved public app (beyond your own install-and-test)? Is there an install cap? Neither is documented.
PKCE support isn't documented; the token exchange uses client_secret over HTTP Basic auth.
Exact Composio callback path (v1 auth-apps/add vs a v3 path): copy it from your Composio dashboard.
The specific terms of the Developer Partner Agreement weren't reviewed.
It's not stated whether a free sandbox is enough or a paid plan is needed for a public listing.
Typical review turnaround beyond the 21-business-day figure, and the number of review rounds, aren't documented.
